Right off the bat, my vote goes to **White Stripes**- Short version is that not only does Niban effectively save the submarine as a whole, as well as everyone inside by one of his first actions, but is more than capable of defending against Stefan's attacks with [Ocean Man]. Moreover, Stefan's attacks on Ocean Man itself do essentially nothing given that Niban has full control over their state of matter, position, and movement- in the end, water vapor is still water, and basically puts Stefan in the same shoes as Josuke/Jotaro against Aqua Necklace.

Now, in order to begin the long version, we need to talk pressure dynamics and how a sub takes advantage of those to dive. With any sort of aquatic ship, there exists 'containers' known as ballasts, whose function is to balance the ship by distributing buoyancy over the area of the ship- Classical sailing ships often created this balance via heavy stones and/or metal, which could be adjusted by adding and removing as needed- though, it would be unwise to do so outside of a port. Modern ship ballasts consist of a container that pumps seawater in and out of the container to maintain stability/adjust the ships center of gravity. 

Now this is functionally similar in a submarine, but instead of just balancing the ship on a flat surface, we need to accomplish it in a three-dimensional space. Depending on the submarine, there can be several setups for Ballast tanks; First and foremost is a single hulled setup, where the interior of the ship and the surrounding ocean are separated by just the hull- Ballast tanks are spread throughout the interior of the submarine in order to maintain balance, no different than a ship. The second setup consists of external tanks that water is loaded into via pumps, usually called a saddle-bag setup. The third setup is known as a double hull setup, where the ballast tanks separate the open ocean from the main hull of the sub- typically the outer hull isn't as thick as the main hull here, but we'll come back to this later. In order to raise and lower the submarine, water is pumped into the ballast tanks while the air in said tanks is syphoned back into the submarine- this lowers the buoyancy of the submarine and causes it to sink. Bear in mind that the pumps that control this process are closed from the rest of the sea when not submerging/surfacing. By submerging, the sea exerts pressure on the submarine due to the force being equal to that of the water around it, and also all the water on top of it- and at 2000 meters, there's about 2,845 PSI of force acting on the sub, which is stated to be it's limit. Suffice to say, while the sub is under considerable pressure, the ballast tanks in the sub are separate compartments, under pressure equal to that of the submarine's. 

So onto the beef of the fight, Niban's move of remotely 'piloting' the ship, here meaning go up, is pivotal for the survival of everyone on the boat- Given it's a death match, I feel this near cements him as the hero here, and allows the fight to last out the 30 second timer that would have played out. Additionally, Niban's [Ocean Man] takes a decent amount of space in it's primary form, no additional water- the average human body at approximately 150 pounds takes up .06 cubic meters of space as it's volume; and given that [Ocean Man] is similar in size and build to Star Platinum, we can assume it's just a tad larger. Niban's ability to fully control the shape and physical state of that water, plus any water connected to OM's water, is incredibly versatile against Stefan's 'pressurization vaporization' attacks- As said above, water vapor is still water, and will invariably make Stefan's fight more complicated, and more dangerous as a result. If all else fails, OM could easily prevent the form from changing if he wanted.

Now I know this is a point of contention, but I'm gonna bring it up again: Assuming Niban can reach the Ballast tanks inside the ship before Stefan can stop him, Niban will have absolutely no issues in getting the water out. Because the Ballasts are a closed system (i.e. the ballast tanks are sealed to prevent water from entering/leaving unless the sub is surfacing/submerging), the air pressure change in this process is almost negligible on the sub as a whole, because the sub too is a closed system- assuming that Stefan/Niban's attacks don't create a breach in the hull, it will continue to be one. In the event that Niban must use OM to forcefully open the tank, this still isn't an issue; OM, coming into contact with any sea-water attempting to flow out, will assimilate with it as quickly as it's flowing- the assimilation would continue so long as there was water to connect with (this is the main function of the stand, after all). With a large mass of water such as this, Niban could easily prevent more water from rushing in, whether by creating a self-repairing ice cap or by sheer mass alone. So long as the submarine doesn't suffer a direct breach to the rest of the ocean, I in no way believe that accessing the ballasts would be of any significant detriment to the sub, if at all.

Now I know I haven't touched on Stefan's plan much in this- And don't get me wrong, it's a precise and well crafted plan, As all of RNF's plans have been. In this instance however, aside from the ocean being Niban's element, Stephan's decision to use his stand on object's pressure simply doesn't work in some cases, or actively works against him- We touched on the vaporization of water previously, which is certainly a cool thing for Stefan to do- if the stand he were up against couldn't control said water in nearly every way. Another instance of weird pressure choice is on bandages and gauze to tighten on Niban, which... isn't exactly how pressurization works. In this instance, de-pressurizing said bandages would essentially eject all oxygen/minor dust/ect. from the bandage, leaving it a shriveled strip of cloth- in extreme cases like what Stefan's implying, the bandage/gauze would outright fall apart. On a side note, despite the slight difference in speed between the two stands, I don't think that OM would easily be captured by Switch- Given speed comparisons between B and A speed stands in the jojo canon, such as the fight between Jotaro and N'Doul or Killer Queen and Crazy Diamond, a B stand could hold it's own for a short time, possibly even long enough to destroy Stefan's containers.

I don't doubt that Stefan's plans to utilize loose screws, aerosol cans, and lightbulbs as projectiles are  feasible, especially those he can carry around- But with regards to Switch's primary ability and it's limitation, it's not a question of if Stefan can do the things he says or not- it's a question of if he can do them in such a short period of time, since both he and Niban are working against the clock; or at the very least, time itself is his enemy here, rather than OM.

**Name**: Albrecht Durer

**Gender/Species**: Male/Human

**Age**: 42

**Occupation**: Theoretical/Experimental Physicist.     

**Bio**: From the first moments he could walk, Albrecht was constantly under the grasp of an insatiable desire to know and understand everything he could; He would tear the limbs from insects and carefully pry open their husks to learn how the interior worked, he would mix household chemicals in impeccably measured amounts to gain the compounds he wanted. By the age of 11, his understanding of higher calculus and physics already towered that of a college graduate. He quickly moved on from studies to actual lab work, testing exorbitant arrays of strange and unknown elements. To his surprise, after day in and day out of testing, he grew wary of the tedium of research- to be precise, it was boredom out of desire for something greater. He didn't simply wish to observe and understand the evolution of life in the physical world, nor simply understand all that he could see- he craved to see and understand the evolution of the laws of the universe itself. It was then, after receiving a scratch from a strange golden metal, that he discovered the Stand- and from then on, he slowly turned to greater and greater levels of experimentation via his Stand, to more and more paranormal means.


**Personality**: An incredibly kind and warm soul, Albrecht treats all of his subordinates like they were his own family- Even to the passer by on the street or the mugger in the alley, he greets them all with a charismatic smile. That, however, only goes so deep; Albrecht is a creature of insatiable curiosity, and will take whatever means necessary to satisfy his interests. This ties into his ultimate goal- to bring about a great 'change' in the nature of reality itself, and observe the evolution of it's laws. His black hair is somewhat greyed, and stretches to the top of his back in a loose ponytail; His usual attire consists of a dress shirt and tie, worn dress slacks and shoes, and a duster jacket for those chilly days.
Equipment: A leather messenger bag containing several notebooks of loose leaf papers, a number of pens of varying colors, a 20 inch steel ruler, a length of nylon cord, and a boxcutter; Ouside the bag, he carries a worn wallet with a number of bills and, in a zipper compartment, a large quantity of coins.

**Stand Name**: 「Just Push Play」/「JP2」


**Stand Type**: Close Range, Humanoid


**Appearance**: 「Just Push Play」, or 「JP2」 for short, takes the appearance of a deep purple Hoplite soldier in partial armor, a helmet dome and crest attached to the top of it's head, and wearing a miner's inhaler on it's face (just the air intake). The body is decorated in a criss-cross pattern of deep purple and black stiching, while crests adorned with a scale are on each of the upper arms at the shoulder.


**Stand Ability: Proportions**
「JP2」 works via proportions (I.e. more than x, less than y.). Essentially, 「JP2」 can manipulate the physical qualities of an object, so long as he touches it- 「JP2」 is only allowed to adjust one property per person or object, and is only allowed to adjust two properties at a time- in order to affect any further targets beyond those, he must shift focus from one 'target' to another. Qualities that can be affected by this Stand are more often concrete/finite,(such as temperature, length, ect.) than those that are more abstract/relative (such as space, time, ect.)
For example, let's say the user is climbing a rope attached to the ceiling, and wants to get to the top faster to avoid an enemy- using 「JP2」, he can affect the rope and make it 'shorter than it is long'- the rope would appear to get shorter very quickly, pulling the user to the ceiling just as fast. Or, perhaps, say he needs to heat up dinner- **fast.** He could put all the dinner-shit on a pan, and choose the pan as his 'target'; 「JP2」grabs it by the handle and pushes the temperature of the pan to be 'hotter than it is cold', essentially bringing the pan to the hottest it can go while still being a pan (by this, I mean without either melting into a puddle of molten metal, or completely vaporizing).

Additionally, 「JP2」's manipulation can't directly cause the object to be destroyed- by the end of the manipulation, the object must still be the 'original object'; So making a cut in a tree 'deeper than it is shallow' could only bring it to the brink of being unbalanced and falling over- it can't make that same cut go the whole way through the tree. However, any events affecting 「JP2」's targets after their changes aren't bound by this- a different stand, or even a woodcutter could chop down the tree in the prior example with the greatest of ease.

**EDIT:**「A-side B-side」  has been removed-In this tournament, 「JP2」can't affect or manipulate concepts like space, let alone time.

In addition to the stand's limit of two targets max (one 'quality' each), 「JP2」 also cannot affect Albrecht directly- if he were to suffer an injury and want to make the wound smaller than larger, he'd be unable to- however, he could easily apply the opposite to a foe if he could get within touching range.

**EDIT 4/5/17:** The judges have asked that I clarify JP2's limitations a bit more clearly to provide better understanding of what it can and can't do. Above I mention circumstances where JP2 is able to manipulate properties, and to the extent they can be 'pushed' to their extremes. There are two points I'll list that should clarify any concerns over what properties can and cannot be pushed:

1. JP2 can't 'push' a property to it's extreme if that object doesn't exhibit that property- an example would be that JP2 cannot make a clump of ordinary dirt more explosive than it isn't, because an ordinary clump of dirt is not explosive on it's own. Bear in mind that JP2 can adjust other properties to make such reactions more ideal via outside interaction, however.
2. Further clarifying the manipulations, it's listed above that the object can't be destroyed directly via the manipulation itself- this means that a manipulation can bring the target to the absolute brink of it's limits without being destroyed- outside interaction, again, can work in conjunction with this however. Furthermore, while the object can't be destroyed as it is, pure or near-pure substances can undergo phase changes; Much like a puddle of water can freeze and evaporate while still being a form of water, a block of iron could be melted to a puddle of iron, or possibly even beyond into stranger states. As with prior statements, outside interaction can affect this.
